serialization_and_reader.CPU_projection: Original CPU tensors total 104MB. Writer/readback may coexist with an additional mapped/restored tensor set and serialization/hash copies; chain validation and unique checks allocate further index/coordinate scratch. Existing host reader uses memmaps and bounded reads, but library/native sort/serializer workspace is not established as a strict peak by this source audit. Qualify full-sized CPU writer/reader with actual metadata before any runtime.
serialization_and_reader.version_note: The Windows safetensors source was read without importing it; its pointer-based save implementation does not establish the exact WSL package implementation. No zero-copy or measured peak claim is made.

integer_and_converter_bounds.conclusion: Existing int32 coordinates/vertex indices, uint32 neighbor indices/sentinel and int64 CPU keys/index arithmetic have ample representational capacity. No coordinate or neighbor rebasing is required.
integer_and_converter_bounds.reason: At most three flagged quads per original row, two triangles per quad; flags and valid-neighbor surface counts are still unknown.
integer_and_converter_bounds.CPU_mesh_projection: Full memmaps, transformed features, coordinate copies, keys/sort buffers, batched neighbors and list-plus-concatenated faces coexist. Source-visible arrays remain far below the 12GiB host floor, but this is not a measured process peak or proof of final topology. Any new face bound must account for the worst case or fail closed explicitly.
